settings.heading: What you are dealing with
settings.intro: You may recognise several of these.
items: You have no clear position on AI. You hear about it every day and cannot say which parts apply to your work.
You tried it and stopped. The answers were average, it took longer than doing the work yourself, and you went back to the old way.
Your inbox sets your day. You read, sort and answer messages that follow the same patterns every week.
You prepare for meetings in the minutes before them. The background is spread across emails, notes and files.
You write the same things again and again. Updates, replies and briefs start from a blank page each time.
Long documents wait for you. Contracts, proposals and reports pile up because reading them properly takes an hour you do not have.
Reports are put together by hand. The figures come from several places, and someone spends hours joining them.
You worry about confidentiality. You do not know what is safe to paste into an AI tool, and nobody has given you a rule.
Your team uses AI in their own ways. You cannot tell what is safe, what is good and what is worth keeping.
Courses assume time you do not have. Every tutorial asks for hours of learning before you see any benefit.
Decisions wait on you. The briefing you needed was not ready when the decision was.
You suspect others are ahead. You cannot judge whether the gap is real, because nobody gives you a straight comparison.

settings.heading: Six things, running on your own accounts
settings.intro: At the end of the two hours you have this. Which ones we set up depends on your work. In the first ten minutes we pick the three that matter most to you.

items.title: An inbox routine
items.text: AI reads and sorts your mail and drafts replies to routine messages in your style. You review everything before it is sent.

items.title: A way through long documents
items.text: Contracts, proposals and reports come back summarised, with the points that need your attention marked.

items.title: Drafting from your voice
items.text: Updates, replies and briefs arrive as drafts to edit, not blank pages.

items.title: Written rules on sharing
items.text: What you can share with AI tools, fitted to your situation.

items.title: A one-page summary
items.text: Your setup and how to use it, so it still works next month.

items.q: How much of my time does it take?
items.a: 30 minutes to fill in a form before the session, then two hours of your attention. That is 2.5 hours, once.
No. You need nothing installed in advance and nothing to read or watch first. You bring your laptop and access to your email and calendar.

items.q: Is there a monthly cost for the tools?

Each Jump needs preparation before and a written summary after, and I do both myself. When the 8 places are taken, the next place is in the following month. I do not add extra sessions.
If you want the work done for you, book an AI Sprint within 7 days and your 2,000 AED is credited in full. Sprint start dates are limited to four a month, always on a Monday.
